what: class-level external validation of the generality engine vs published network meta-analyses
method: engine ranking/lead read programmatically from each class league JSON; concordance judged at class-direction / top-tier / no-clean-winner level (not numeric effect match); every reference DOI resolved on PubMed.

entries.published_finding: Among PCSK9i monotherapy vs placebo, LDL-C reduction ranked evolocumab (MD -1.89) > alirocumab (-1.83) > inclisiran (-1.68 mmol/L).
entries.our_finding: engine ranks the overlapping agents evolocumab > alirocumab > inclisiran (lead overall bococizumab, a withdrawn agent NOT in the published network).

concordance.basis: inclisiran ranks last among the three shared agents in BOTH analyses; PCSK9i all lower LDL-C.
concordance.honest_note: our overall lead bococizumab was withdrawn and is absent from the published network; comparison is restricted to the evolocumab/alirocumab/inclisiran overlap. Jiang pools combination arms; we model %LDL monotherapy.

entries.published_finding: SGLT-2 inhibitors reduced heart-failure hospitalisation (and end-stage renal disease) as a class; no clean within-class efficacy winner is crowned.
entries.our_finding: engine: all SGLT2 agents reduce HF hospitalisation (lead canagliflozin HR 0.67), but every contrast is Low/Very-low certainty -> no clean within-class winner.

concordance.basis: class-level direction matches (SGLT2i reduce HF hosp); both decline to crown a within-class winner.
concordance.honest_note: Tsapas is a broad glucose-lowering NMA reporting SGLT2i at class level, not a canagliflozin-vs-empagliflozin-vs-dapagliflozin head-to-head; our nominal canagliflozin lead is explicitly Low-certainty, consistent with that.

honest_boundary: this is corroboration at the level the abstracts support, not a re-pooling of the published data; contrasts differ across analyses and each entry records its boundary. Registry-native (AACT) engine vs full-SR published NMAs.
